title: Airgap supply-chain attestation and bundle signing notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working note collects an initial design and operational checklist for securing and verifying artifact supply chains for air-gapped/private deployments. Focus: container images, helm charts, OCI blobs and model bundles (weights + tokenizer + config). Goal: make offline installs auditable and automatable with a small trusted verification surface.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers deploying Redwood Private in sealed networks require deterministic, verifiable artifact bundles.
- Existing mirror playbooks ensure mirror consistency but do not standardize attestation, signature rotation, or SBOM consumption for model artifacts.
- Upgrades are currently brittle when bundle provenance is not machine-verifiable. We need a repeatable flow for CI->staging->mirror->install that includes signatures and checksums.

High-level design principles:
1) Single-source attestation: each release bundle produced by CI must include an SBOM, a checksum manifest, and a detached signature from a signing key guarded in KMS/HSM.
2) Minimal offline verifier: the installer (airgap bootstrap) only needs a small set of root public keys and a verification binary (cosign or a thin shim) to validate everything.
3) Immutable bundle layout: tarball layout and naming must be stable across releases to simplify checks and delta upgrades.
4) Rotations and revocation: plan for key rotation, CRL-style revocation files included in signed manifests.
5) Clear rollback paths: upgrade plan must include a validated rollback bundle, sign-off checklist, and automated sanity checks post-upgrade.

Bundle contents (recommended canonical layout):
- /release-M.m.p/
  - bundle.tar.gz  (contains images/ charts/ models/ manifests/)
  - checksums.sha256 (lines: <sha256>  bundle.tar.gz)
  - sbom.spdx.json (spdx v2.2 minimal fields for images and libs)
  - signatures/
     - bundle.tar.gz.sig (cosign detached signature or kms-encrypted envelope)
     - checksums.sha256.sig
  - release-metadata.yaml (version, build-id, git-ref, build-timestamp, supported-configs)
  - attestation.json (optional in-toto predicate describing build environment)

Signing & attestation recommendations:
- Use cosign for OCI artifacts and detached signatures for bundle.tar.gz and checksums. Where customers demand HSM-backed keys, integrate with KMS; generate a signing envelope that cosign can verify.
- Produce an in-toto attestation for model artifact provenance (build pipeline, hash of training checkpoint id if applicable).
- Include signature verification steps in CI so that every published bundle has passing verification in an isolated runner.

Checksum and SBOM rules:
- checksums.sha256 must cover every file in the bundle root with explicit file paths.
- For model weights, include both file-level checksums and a model-manifest with architecture, format (e.g., gguf, ggml, pt), tokenizer hash.
- SBOM should map images and key third-party libraries; include sha256 for container images as recorded in the OCI manifest.

Terraform module notes (variables & interfaces for mirror operator):
- Variables proposed: mirror_registry_endpoint, mirror_namespace, allow_push_from_central, bundle_source_uri (gs:// or s3:// or artifact registry URL), trusted_root_keys (list of public key fingerprints), verify_with_cosign (bool), rotation_policy (days).
- Suggested outputs: last_sync_time, last_verified_bundle, broken_files_count, current_index_sha256.
- Operator should expose a "verify_bundle" lifecycle action which: downloads bundle -> validates checksums -> validates signatures against trusted_root_keys -> verifies SBOM presence -> produces a verification report artifact.
- For Terraform testing, provide a local-exec hook that runs a containerized verifier (cosign + sbom-verify) so infra changes can be validated during CI.

Mirror topology and operational flow:
1) CI publishes signed bundle to a staging GCS/S3 location and creates a signed index.json (index includes bundle version, checksum, signature).
2) Transfer mechanism options: rsync over jump host, signed USB (sneakernet) for high-security customers, or an authenticated artifact-sync operator that pulls into Harbor/AzureACR/Artifactory offline registry.
3) Mirror operator downloads bundle to staging mirror, runs "verify_bundle", then loads OCI images into local registry and extracts charts/models into blob store.
4) After successful verification, operator flips traffic or marks bundle available to the installer catalog.

Upgrade plan (air-gapped):
- Pre-upgrade: verify current cluster state, snapshot relevant PVs, ensure current bundle metadata and rollback bundle are present locally.
- Upgrade steps:
  1. Run local verifier against the new bundle index and checksums.
  2. Check signatures against trusted roots; run sbom diff to detect unexpected new dependencies.
  3. Deploy to canary nodes (node-pool labeled canary) using the local charts.
  4. Run smoke tests + model sanity checks (short prompt regressions) using local test harness.
  5. If all green, rollout to remaining nodes with staged parallelism and resource throttling.
- Post-upgrade verification: token billing sanity, latency percentiles, healthchecks, and a signed post-upgrade attest file placed in /var/lib/redwood/attestations/.
- Rollback: Plan to re-apply previous signed bundle tarball and run the same verification flow. Ensure operator keeps last N (suggest N=3) verified bundles locally.

Verification checklist (run manually or automated step):
- [ ] checksums.sha256 exists and matches bundle contents
- [ ] detached signatures exist for bundle + checksums
- [ ] cosign verification passes against local root key(s)
- [ ] sbom present and parsed without critical unknown licenses
- [ ] model-manifest verified (format + tokenizer hash)
- [ ] in-toto predicate (if present) validates builder identity
- [ ] index.json signature valid and timestamp within allowed window

Key rotation and revocation:
- Rotation strategy: maintain a signing transition window. New bundles signed by new key + old key until cutoff date. Installer trusts both until rotation complete.
- Revocation: publish a signed revocation list as revocations.json; verifier must consult this list during verification. For extreme cases, provide a revocation CRL that blocks specific build-ids.

Edge cases and gotchas:
- Large model tarballs may push memory when computing checksums; verifier should stream and use chunked hashing.
- If using compressed tarballs, ensure canonical ordering before computing checksums (deterministic tar creation).
- Time skew in sealed environments: use signed timestamps in release-metadata and tolerate up to a configurable drift.
- Network partitions during mirror sync: partial transfers should be quarantined; only accept bundles that pass verification end-to-end.

Operational playbook snippet (short runbook):
- "mirror-verify-and-serve" (operator runbook):
  1) pull bundle from source location to /var/cache/redwood/bundles/<version>/incoming
  2) run /opt/redwood/bin/bundle-verify --bundle /var/cache/redwood/bundles/<version>/bundle.tar.gz --roots /etc/redwood/roots.pem
  3) if verify ok, extract -> load images: /opt/redwood/bin/load-images --registry localhost:5000 --namespace redwood
  4) publish catalog entry: POST to local catalog API with signed index and verification report
  5) alert #eng-private-deployments Slack with short verification digest

TODOs and open questions:
- Decide canonical SBOM format (SPDX v2.2 vs CycloneDX) for model bundles; customer legal teams sometimes prefer one over the other.
- Define maximum acceptable time window for signed metadata timestamp drift.
- Standardize a minimal in-toto predicate for model training provenance (what fields are required).
- UX for customers: provide a small verification toolkit packaged as a static binary for air-gapped customers who cannot run containers during verification.

References and quick commands:
- cosign verify: cosign verify --key <public.pem> bundle.tar.gz.sig
- generate checksums: sha256sum bundle.tar.gz > checksums.sha256
- sample terraform var use: variable "trusted_root_keys" { type = list(string) description = "cosign public key fingerprints allowed for bundle verification" default = ["sha256:abc..."] }

Notes: this doc is intentionally operational and compact — aim is to convert into a formal runbook and a Terraform module README where the verification binary/containers and example CI pipeline are included.

Signed-off-by: Miguel Torres (eng-private-deployments)
